doc.title: Larry Ridley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 10, 2003

title: Rutgers politics, kindred spirits and goodbyes
summary: Closing talk of institutional politics and teamwork, and mutual thanks.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well thank you. And thank you again for taking the time and asking me to be a part of this. And we have to — you know you have a voice in working with us too. Because you are a sincere and dedicated person. And we need your energies and we need your expertise, you know like to bring your ideas to us. Because it’s about a team. Networking. And working together works. And we need serious, dedicated people. And everybody’s going to get their little niche. I know everybody’s got their own little personal thing and their own little parochial turfs and parochial politics, you know we’ve all experienced that. God knows I went through it at Rutgers. MR I’ll bet.
And the professors, we called it the Rutgers Screw. Yes, you know what I’m talking about.
It happens at every institution. Right?

But the point is keeping our eyes on the prize and recognizing that we are kindred spirits and that we seek out each other and we have mutual empathy about what it is that we’re trying to do and we’re not alone. Sometimes we feel like we’re alone, but we’re really aren’t alone. We just have to expose ourselves to forums and venues where we can have the opportunity, just like we’re doing right now. You didn’t know much about me other than what you read on the page. Now I hope you have a little more insight into Larry Ridley the human being.
And that’s just the tip of the iceberg.
